name: General Physician
alias: Your family doctor for everyday illness
keywords: fever flu cough cold bp blood pressure sugar checkup infection body pain typhoid dengue weakness
intro: A general physician is your first stop for most health problems. They diagnose and treat common illnesses, manage long-term conditions like blood pressure and diabetes, and refer you to the right specialist when you need one.

services.name: General consultation
services.desc: Examination, diagnosis and a treatment plan for new symptoms.

services.name: Full body checkup
services.desc: Blood tests, BP and sugar, with a review of your results.

services.name: BP and sugar follow-ups
services.desc: Regular visits to keep long-term conditions under control.

services.name: Adult vaccinations
services.desc: Flu, hepatitis B, typhoid and travel vaccines.

services.name: Medical certificates
services.desc: Fitness, sick-leave and pre-employment certificates.

services.name: Home visits
services.desc: Doctor visits for elderly or bedridden patients, where available.

signs: A fever that lasts more than three days
A cough that doesn't settle after two weeks
Feeling tired or weak for no clear reason
BP or sugar readings outside your usual range
You're not sure which specialist to see

faqs.q: Should I see a general physician or a specialist first?
faqs.a: Start with a general physician unless you already know the problem needs a specialist. They can treat most conditions and will refer you if needed, which often saves time and money.

faqs.q: What should I bring to my appointment?
faqs.a: Bring your CNIC, any previous prescriptions, recent test reports and a list of the medicines you take.

faqs.q: How often should I get a full checkup?
faqs.a: Once a year is a good habit for adults over 30, or more often if you have diabetes, high blood pressure or heart disease in the family.

faqs.q: Can I book a same-day appointment?
faqs.a: Yes. Most general physicians listed here have same-day evening slots. Choose Today when you book.

name: Dermatology
keywords: skin acne pimples hair fall baldness eczema pigmentation melasma freckles laser rash itching fungal nails scars whitening
intro: Dermatologists treat conditions of the skin, hair and nails, from acne and allergies to hair loss and pigmentation. Many also offer cosmetic procedures such as laser, chemical peels and PRP.

services.name: Skin consultation
services.desc: Diagnosis and a treatment plan for skin, hair or nail problems.

services.name: Chemical peels
services.desc: Treats acne marks, dullness and uneven skin tone.

services.name: Laser hair removal
services.desc: Long-term reduction of unwanted hair over several sessions.

services.name: PRP for hair loss
services.desc: Uses your own platelets to support hair regrowth.

services.name: Acne scar treatment
services.desc: Microneedling, laser or subcision, depending on the scar type.

services.name: Mole and wart removal
services.desc: Quick in-clinic removal with cautery or cryotherapy.

signs: Acne that hasn't improved with over-the-counter products
Hair falling out in patches or thinning quickly
A mole that changes size, shape or colour
A rash or itching that lasts more than a week
Dark patches spreading on your face

faqs.q: How many sessions does laser hair removal take?
faqs.a: Most people need 6 to 8 sessions, four to six weeks apart. Your dermatologist will advise based on your skin and hair type.

faqs.q: Is PRP safe?
faqs.a: PRP uses your own blood, so allergic reactions are rare. Mild redness or soreness for a day is normal.

faqs.q: Can I use whitening creams?
faqs.a: Avoid creams that weren't prescribed. Many contain strong steroids or mercury that can damage your skin. A dermatologist can recommend safe treatment for pigmentation.

faqs.q: When will I see results for acne?
faqs.a: Most acne treatments take 6 to 8 weeks to show clear improvement. Keep using them as prescribed, even if progress feels slow.

name: Dental Care
keywords: teeth tooth toothache dentist cavity filling root canal braces scaling cleaning whitening gums bleeding implant wisdom
intro: Dentists look after your teeth and gums. They treat pain, decay and infection, and offer cleaning, braces and cosmetic work to improve your smile.

services.name: Scaling and polishing
services.desc: Removes plaque and tartar to keep your gums healthy.

services.name: Fillings
services.desc: Tooth-coloured fillings to repair cavities.

services.name: Root canal treatment
services.desc: Saves an infected tooth and stops the pain.

services.name: Braces and aligners
services.desc: Straightens teeth with metal, ceramic or clear aligners.

services.name: Teeth whitening
services.desc: In-clinic whitening for a brighter smile in one visit.

services.name: Dental implants
services.desc: A permanent replacement for missing teeth.

signs: Tooth pain that keeps you up at night
Gums that bleed when you brush
Swelling in your face or jaw
Sensitivity to hot or cold that won't go away
It's been more than six months since your last checkup

faqs.q: Is root canal treatment painful?
faqs.a: It's done under local anaesthesia, so it should feel similar to a filling. Some soreness for a few days afterwards is normal.

faqs.q: How often should I get my teeth cleaned?
faqs.a: Every six months for most people, or more often if you have gum disease.

faqs.q: At what age can children get braces?
faqs.a: Orthodontists usually assess children around age 7, and most braces are fitted between 10 and 14.

faqs.q: How long do implants last?
faqs.a: With good care, an implant can last 20 years or more.

name: Gynecology and Obstetrics
keywords: pregnancy pregnant periods menstrual pcos pcod infertility gynae gynaecologist women delivery c-section ultrasound pap smear menopause
intro: Gynecologists care for women's reproductive health, from periods and PCOS to fertility and menopause. Obstetricians look after you through pregnancy and delivery. Most doctors listed here practise both.

services.name: Antenatal checkups
services.desc: Regular visits, scans and tests through each trimester.

services.name: Pregnancy ultrasound
services.desc: Dating, anomaly and growth scans.

services.name: Normal and C-section delivery
services.desc: Delivery at partner hospitals with a doctor you know.

services.name: PCOS management
services.desc: Diet, medicine and follow-up to regulate cycles and symptoms.

services.name: Fertility consultation
services.desc: Tests and treatment options for couples trying to conceive.

services.name: Pap smear screening
services.desc: Early screening for cervical cancer.

signs: Periods that are very heavy, painful or irregular
You're planning a pregnancy or think you're pregnant
Unusual discharge, itching or pelvic pain
Trying to conceive for over a year without success
Bleeding after menopause

faqs.q: When should I book my first pregnancy visit?
faqs.a: As soon as you have a positive test, ideally by 8 weeks. Early visits confirm the pregnancy and start folic acid and other care on time.

faqs.q: Can I choose a female doctor?
faqs.a: Yes. Every gynecologist listed on this page is female.

faqs.q: Can PCOS be cured?
faqs.a: PCOS can't be cured, but its symptoms can be controlled well with lifestyle changes and medicine.

faqs.q: How often do I need a Pap smear?
faqs.a: Every three years for women aged 25 to 65, or as your doctor advises.

name: Pediatrics
alias: Health care for babies, children and teens
keywords: child children baby kids infant newborn vaccination vaccine fever diarrhea diarrhoea growth paeds pediatric cough jaundice
intro: Pediatricians care for children from birth to 18. They treat childhood illnesses, track growth and development, and keep vaccinations on schedule.

services.name: Well-baby checkups
services.desc: Growth, feeding and development checks in the first years.

services.name: Vaccinations
services.desc: EPI and optional vaccines, with a reminder before each dose.

services.name: Newborn care
services.desc: Jaundice checks, feeding support and first-month visits.

services.name: Growth and nutrition
services.desc: Height and weight tracking with diet advice.

services.name: Asthma and allergy care
services.desc: Inhaler plans and allergy management for children.

services.name: Development assessment
services.desc: Checks for speech, movement and learning milestones.

signs: A baby under three months with any fever
A fever over 102°F (39°C) that won't come down
Your child isn't eating, drinking or passing urine
Fast or difficult breathing
Missed vaccinations you want to catch up on
alert: If your child is drowsy and hard to wake, has a seizure, or is struggling to breathe, call 1122 or go to the nearest emergency department.

faqs.q: Which vaccines are free in Pakistan?
faqs.a: The government EPI programme covers core vaccines such as BCG, polio, pentavalent, pneumococcal, rotavirus, measles and typhoid. Your pediatrician can also advise on optional vaccines.

faqs.q: How often should my baby see a pediatrician?
faqs.a: Usually at 1 to 2 weeks, then alongside each vaccine visit, and every few months after that in the first two years.

faqs.q: My child has a fever. When should I worry?
faqs.a: See a doctor quickly if your baby is under three months, the fever lasts more than two days, or your child is drowsy, has a rash or has trouble breathing.

faqs.q: Up to what age does a child see a pediatrician?
faqs.a: Most pediatricians see children up to 18 years old.

name: Orthopedics
keywords: bone bones joint joints knee pain back pain spine fracture arthritis shoulder neck sports injury ligament slip disc
intro: Orthopedic surgeons treat problems of the bones, joints, ligaments and spine, whether from injury, wear and tear or arthritis. Most visits don't lead to surgery; many problems improve with medicine and physiotherapy.

services.name: Orthopedic consultation
services.desc: Examination, X-ray review and a treatment plan.

services.name: Fracture care
services.desc: Plaster, splints or surgery, depending on the break.

services.name: Joint injections
services.desc: Steroid or hyaluronic acid injections for joint pain.

services.name: Knee and hip replacement
services.desc: Surgery for advanced arthritis at partner hospitals.

services.name: Arthroscopy
services.desc: Keyhole surgery for knee and shoulder injuries.

services.name: Spine care
services.desc: Treatment for slip disc and long-term back pain.

signs: Joint pain that lasts more than two weeks
You can't put weight on a leg after a fall
Back pain that spreads down your leg
Swelling or stiffness in the mornings
A joint that locks, clicks or gives way

faqs.q: Do I need an X-ray before my visit?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. The doctor will order the right scan after examining you. Bring any old X-ray or MRI reports you have.

faqs.q: Will I need surgery?
faqs.a: Most bone and joint problems are treated without surgery, using medicine, rest and physiotherapy. Surgery is advised only when these don't work or the injury needs it.

faqs.q: How long does a fracture take to heal?
faqs.a: Most fractures heal in 6 to 12 weeks, depending on the bone and your age.

faqs.q: Should I see an orthopedic surgeon or a physiotherapist for back pain?
faqs.a: See an orthopedic surgeon first if the pain followed an injury, spreads down your leg or comes with numbness. For a muscle strain, a physiotherapist is often enough.

name: ENT
keywords: ear nose throat ent sinus tonsils hearing loss ear pain ringing tinnitus snoring voice allergy nosebleed vertigo
intro: ENT specialists treat problems of the ear, nose, throat and neck, including sinus trouble, tonsils, hearing loss and snoring.

services.name: ENT consultation
services.desc: Examination of the ear, nose and throat with a lighted scope.

services.name: Ear wax removal
services.desc: Safe removal by suction or irrigation.

services.name: Hearing test
services.desc: Audiometry to measure hearing in each ear.

services.name: Nasal endoscopy
services.desc: A camera check for sinus and nasal problems.

services.name: Tonsil and adenoid surgery
services.desc: For repeated infections or breathing problems in children.

services.name: Sinus surgery
services.desc: Endoscopic surgery when sinus problems don't settle with medicine.

signs: Ear pain or discharge
A sore throat that keeps coming back
A blocked nose for more than ten days
Sudden loss of hearing in one ear
Hoarseness lasting more than three weeks

faqs.q: Should I clean my ears with cotton buds?
faqs.a: No. Buds push wax deeper and can injure the eardrum. If your ear feels blocked, have it cleaned at a clinic.

faqs.q: When are tonsils removed?
faqs.a: Usually when a child has many throat infections in a year, or when large tonsils cause snoring or pauses in breathing during sleep.

faqs.q: Is sudden hearing loss an emergency?
faqs.a: Yes. Sudden hearing loss in one ear should be seen within 24 to 48 hours, because early treatment improves recovery.

faqs.q: Can allergies cause sinus problems?
faqs.a: Yes. Nasal allergies are a common cause of blocked sinuses, and treating the allergy often helps.

name: Eye Care
keywords: eye eyes vision sight glasses spectacles cataract lasik red eye squint glaucoma lens contact blurry ophthalmologist
intro: Eye specialists (ophthalmologists) are doctors who treat eye disease and perform eye surgery. They check your vision, prescribe glasses and lenses, and treat conditions like cataract and glaucoma.

services.name: Eye exam and vision test
services.desc: Checks eyesight and eye health in one visit.

services.name: Glasses and lens prescription
services.desc: Accurate power for glasses or contact lenses.

services.name: Cataract surgery
services.desc: Phaco surgery with a lens implant, usually same-day.

services.name: LASIK
services.desc: Laser surgery to reduce or remove the need for glasses.

services.name: Glaucoma screening
services.desc: Eye pressure and optic nerve checks.

services.name: Retina checkup
services.desc: Screening for diabetic and age-related retina problems.

signs: Blurry vision or trouble reading
Sudden loss of vision or flashes of light
Red, painful eyes
You have diabetes and haven't had an eye check this year
Frequent headaches when reading or using screens

faqs.q: Am I suitable for LASIK?
faqs.a: Usually, if you're over 18, your glasses power has been stable for a year and your cornea is thick enough. A pre-LASIK test will confirm it.

faqs.q: How long is recovery after cataract surgery?
faqs.a: Most people see clearly within a few days and return to normal activities within a week.

faqs.q: How often should children have an eye test?
faqs.a: Before starting school, and then every one to two years.

faqs.q: Do I need an eye check if I have diabetes?
faqs.a: Yes, once a year. Diabetes can damage the retina before you notice any symptoms.

name: Cardiology
keywords: heart chest pain bp blood pressure cholesterol ecg echo palpitations heart attack angina breathless cardiac
intro: Cardiologists diagnose and treat diseases of the heart and blood vessels, including high blood pressure, chest pain, an irregular heartbeat and heart failure.

services.name: Cardiology consultation
services.desc: Assessment of heart symptoms and risk factors.

services.name: ECG
services.desc: A quick test of your heart's rhythm.

services.name: Echocardiography
services.desc: An ultrasound of the heart's structure and pumping.

services.name: Exercise tolerance test
services.desc: Checks your heart while you walk on a treadmill.

services.name: Holter monitoring
services.desc: Records your heart rhythm for 24 to 48 hours.

services.name: Angiography referral
services.desc: Coordination with partner hospitals for angiography and stents.

signs: Chest pain or tightness, especially with exertion
Breathlessness when climbing stairs
A racing or irregular heartbeat
Swelling in your feet and ankles
A family history of heart disease before 55
alert: Severe chest pain, or chest pain with sweating, breathlessness or pain spreading to your arm or jaw, can be a heart attack. Call 1122 or go to the nearest emergency department now.

faqs.q: When is chest pain an emergency?
faqs.a: Call 1122 or go to an emergency department if chest pain is severe, lasts more than a few minutes, or comes with sweating, breathlessness or pain spreading to the arm or jaw.

faqs.q: Do I need to fast before my visit?
faqs.a: Not for a consultation. For a cholesterol test, your doctor may ask you to fast for 9 to 12 hours.

faqs.q: What's the difference between an ECG and an echo?
faqs.a: An ECG records your heart's electrical rhythm in a few minutes. An echo is an ultrasound that shows how the heart muscle and valves are working.

faqs.q: At what age should I get my heart checked?
faqs.a: From 40, or earlier if you smoke or have diabetes, high blood pressure or a family history of heart disease.

name: Physiotherapy
keywords: physio physiotherapy back pain neck pain rehab stroke rehab sports injury exercise posture knee frozen shoulder sciatica
intro: Physiotherapists help you recover movement and strength after injury, surgery or illness, and treat ongoing pain with exercise, hands-on therapy and electrotherapy.

services.name: Physio assessment
services.desc: Movement and strength tests with a personal plan.

services.name: Manual therapy
services.desc: Hands-on treatment for joints and soft tissue.

services.name: Exercise therapy
services.desc: Guided exercises to build strength and flexibility.

services.name: Electrotherapy
services.desc: TENS, ultrasound and heat for pain relief.

services.name: Rehab after surgery
services.desc: Recovery programmes after knee, hip or spine surgery.

services.name: Home physiotherapy
services.desc: Sessions at home for elderly or bedridden patients.

signs: Pain that limits your daily activities
Stiffness after an injury or surgery
Recovering from a stroke
Sports injuries that keep coming back
Pain from long hours at a desk

faqs.q: Do I need a doctor's referral?
faqs.a: No. You can book a physiotherapist directly. Bring any reports or scans you have.

faqs.q: How many sessions will I need?
faqs.a: It depends on the problem. Many people improve within 6 to 10 sessions.

faqs.q: What should I wear?
faqs.a: Loose, comfortable clothes that let you move and give access to the area being treated.

faqs.q: Can physiotherapy help me avoid surgery?
faqs.a: For many back, knee and shoulder problems, yes. Your physiotherapist will tell you if surgery should be considered.

name: Nutrition and Dietetics
alias: Diet plans for weight and health
keywords: diet dietitian nutrition nutritionist weight loss weight gain obesity diet plan food keto pcos diet diabetes diet
intro: Dietitians create food plans that fit your health, culture and routine, whether you want to lose weight, manage diabetes or PCOS, or help your family eat better.

services.name: Diet consultation
services.desc: A review of your eating habits, health and goals.

services.name: Weight loss plan
services.desc: A realistic plan built around the desi food you enjoy.

services.name: Medical nutrition therapy
services.desc: Diet plans for diabetes, kidney and heart conditions.

services.name: Body composition analysis
services.desc: Measures fat, muscle and water, not just weight.

services.name: Online follow-ups
services.desc: Weekly check-ins over video or WhatsApp.

services.name: Family meal planning
services.desc: Healthy meals the whole household can share.

signs: You've tried diets that didn't last
You've been diagnosed with diabetes, PCOS or high cholesterol
Your doctor has asked you to lose weight
You're pregnant and unsure what to eat
Your child is underweight or a picky eater

faqs.q: Will I have to stop eating roti and rice?
faqs.a: No. A good plan adjusts portions and pairings instead of cutting out the foods you eat every day.

faqs.q: How fast will I lose weight?
faqs.a: Half a kilogram to one kilogram a week is a safe, lasting pace for most people.

faqs.q: Is a dietitian the same as a nutritionist?
faqs.a: Dietitians have clinical training to manage diet for medical conditions. If you have a health condition, check that your provider is a qualified dietitian.

faqs.q: Can I consult online?
faqs.a: Yes. Most dietitians listed here offer video consultations and WhatsApp follow-ups.

name: Psychiatry
keywords: mental health anxiety depression stress sleep insomnia panic ocd bipolar psychiatrist psychologist therapy counselling adhd
intro: Psychiatrists are doctors who diagnose and treat mental health conditions with medicine, therapy or both. Asking for help is a normal part of looking after your health, and every visit is confidential.

services.name: Psychiatric consultation
services.desc: A private assessment and treatment plan.

services.name: Medication management
services.desc: Careful prescribing with regular reviews.

services.name: Therapy and counselling
services.desc: Talk therapy with a psychologist, including CBT.

services.name: Online consultation
services.desc: Video sessions from the privacy of your home.

services.name: Child and teen care
services.desc: Support for children's emotional and behavioural concerns.

services.name: Addiction treatment
services.desc: Help to stop smoking, drugs or other dependencies.

signs: Feeling low or hopeless for more than two weeks
Worry or panic that gets in the way of daily life
Trouble sleeping most nights
Losing interest in things you used to enjoy
Thoughts of harming yourself
alert: If you're thinking about harming yourself, please don't wait for an appointment. Call 1122 or go to the nearest hospital emergency department now.

faqs.q: Is my visit confidential?
faqs.a: Yes. Your consultation and records are private and aren't shared without your consent.

faqs.q: What's the difference between a psychiatrist and a psychologist?
faqs.a: A psychiatrist is a medical doctor who can prescribe medicine. A psychologist provides talk therapy and assessments but doesn't prescribe.

faqs.q: Will I have to take medicine forever?
faqs.a: Usually not. Many people take medicine for a set period and stop gradually with their doctor's guidance.

faqs.q: Can I see someone online?
faqs.a: Yes. Most psychiatrists listed here offer video consultations.

name: Diabetes and Endocrinology
keywords: diabetes sugar insulin thyroid hormones endocrinologist hba1c obesity pcos growth vitamin d calcium
intro: Endocrinologists treat conditions caused by hormone problems. Diabetes and thyroid disorders are the most common, along with obesity, PCOS, and bone and growth problems.

services.name: Diabetes consultation
services.desc: Medicine, insulin and a plan to keep your sugar in range.

services.name: Starting insulin
services.desc: Step-by-step training to use insulin with confidence.

services.name: Thyroid clinic
services.desc: Diagnosis and treatment for an underactive or overactive thyroid.

services.name: HbA1c and lab tests
services.desc: Tests that show your average sugar over three months.

services.name: Diabetic foot check
services.desc: Screening to prevent foot ulcers and infections.

services.name: Weight management
services.desc: Medical support for weight loss, including newer medicines where suitable.

signs: Feeling very thirsty and passing urine often
Unexplained weight loss or gain
Sugar readings that stay high despite medicine
Feeling tired and cold, or losing hair
A lump or swelling in your neck

faqs.q: What is a normal HbA1c?
faqs.a: Below 5.7% is normal. 5.7% to 6.4% suggests prediabetes, and 6.5% or above suggests diabetes. Many people with diabetes aim to stay below 7%.

faqs.q: Can type 2 diabetes be reversed?
faqs.a: Some people reach remission with significant weight loss and diet changes. Your doctor can tell you whether this is realistic for you.

faqs.q: Do I need to fast before a thyroid test?
faqs.a: No, fasting usually isn't needed for a thyroid test.

faqs.q: Should I see a general physician or an endocrinologist for diabetes?
faqs.a: Many people manage diabetes well with a general physician. See an endocrinologist if your sugar stays high, you need insulin, or you have complications.

name: Gastroenterology
keywords: stomach gastro acidity heartburn ulcer liver hepatitis jaundice constipation diarrhea ibs piles endoscopy colonoscopy bloating gas
intro: Gastroenterologists treat problems of the digestive system, including the stomach, intestines, liver and pancreas. They also perform endoscopy and colonoscopy.

services.name: Gastro consultation
services.desc: Assessment of digestive symptoms and a treatment plan.

services.name: Upper GI endoscopy
services.desc: A camera test to check the food pipe and stomach.

services.name: Colonoscopy
services.desc: Examines the large bowel for bleeding, polyps or disease.

services.name: Hepatitis treatment
services.desc: Testing and treatment for hepatitis B and C.

services.name: Liver FibroScan
services.desc: Measures liver stiffness and fat without a biopsy.

services.name: H. pylori testing
services.desc: A breath or stool test for a common cause of ulcers.

signs: Heartburn more than twice a week
Difficulty swallowing
Blood in vomit or stool
Yellow eyes or skin
Unexplained weight loss or ongoing tummy pain

faqs.q: Is endoscopy painful?
faqs.a: Endoscopy is done with sedation or a throat spray. Most people feel only mild discomfort and go home the same day.

faqs.q: Can hepatitis C be cured?
faqs.a: Yes. Modern tablets cure hepatitis C in most people within 12 weeks.

faqs.q: What causes fatty liver?
faqs.a: Excess weight, diabetes and high cholesterol are the most common causes. Losing weight is the main treatment.

faqs.q: Do I need to fast before an endoscopy?
faqs.a: Yes, usually for 6 to 8 hours. The clinic will give you exact instructions.

name: Urology
keywords: kidney stone stones urine urinary burning uti bladder prostate urologist male infertility blood in urine incontinence
intro: Urologists treat conditions of the kidneys, bladder and urinary tract in men and women, as well as the male reproductive system.

services.name: Urology consultation
services.desc: Assessment of urinary symptoms and a treatment plan.

services.name: Kidney stone treatment
services.desc: Medicine, ESWL or laser surgery, depending on stone size.

services.name: Ultrasound KUB
services.desc: A scan of the kidneys, ureters and bladder.

services.name: Prostate checkup
services.desc: PSA test and examination for men over 50.

services.name: Cystoscopy
services.desc: A camera check of the bladder.

services.name: Male fertility evaluation
services.desc: Semen analysis and treatment options.

signs: Severe pain in your side or back that comes in waves
Burning or pain when passing urine
Blood in your urine
A weak flow or getting up often at night to urinate
Leaking urine

faqs.q: Can kidney stones pass on their own?
faqs.a: Small stones, under about 5 mm, often pass with water and medicine. Larger stones usually need treatment.

faqs.q: How much water should I drink to prevent stones?
faqs.a: Enough to pass about 2.5 litres of urine a day. For most people that means around 3 litres of fluid, and more in summer.

faqs.q: At what age should men get a prostate check?
faqs.a: Usually from 50, or from 45 if there's a family history of prostate cancer.

faqs.q: Do urologists treat women?
faqs.a: Yes. Urologists treat urinary problems in both men and women.

name: Neurology
keywords: brain nerves neuro migraine headache fits seizures epilepsy stroke paralysis numbness tingling parkinson dementia memory vertigo
intro: Neurologists diagnose and treat disorders of the brain, spinal cord and nerves, such as migraine, epilepsy, stroke and Parkinson's disease.

services.name: Neurology consultation
services.desc: A detailed history and nerve examination.

services.name: EEG
services.desc: Records brain activity to help diagnose epilepsy.

services.name: Nerve conduction study
services.desc: Tests how well your nerves carry signals.

services.name: Stroke follow-up
services.desc: Medicine and rehab plans to prevent another stroke.

services.name: Headache clinic
services.desc: Diagnosis and prevention plans for migraine.

services.name: Memory assessment
services.desc: Tests for early memory problems.

signs: Headaches that are new, severe or getting worse
A seizure or fainting spell
Numbness or weakness on one side of the body
A tremor or slow movement
Memory problems affecting daily life
alert: Sudden face drooping, arm weakness or slurred speech can be a stroke. Call 1122 immediately. Treatment works best in the first few hours.

faqs.q: When is a headache serious?
faqs.a: Get urgent care for the worst headache of your life, a headache with fever and a stiff neck, or a headache after a head injury.

faqs.q: Can epilepsy be controlled?
faqs.a: Most people with epilepsy become seizure-free with the right medicine.

faqs.q: How quickly does a stroke need treatment?
faqs.a: Clot-dissolving treatment works best within 4.5 hours of symptoms starting, so get to hospital immediately.

faqs.q: Do I need an MRI?
faqs.a: Not always. Your neurologist will decide based on your symptoms and examination.
